title: Red test isolation: a failing test stops its area, not the line
summary: Owner direction of 23 November 2026: a failing test must be isolated and must not paralyse the whole system. In about 24 hours four repair cards (AGT-3975, AGT-3980, AGT-3981, AGT-3983) were opened and none was a regression of the blamed merge: two flaky, two environment. The single-run bisect without a control at the last green SHA explains why the newest merge was blamed. Proposal: build, prepare and a small base suite stop the line; any other test failing twice at the same SHA becomes a held quarantine (24 h, one renewal, cap 3 held and 8 total, server-side store) that keeps develop green with a count and holds only cards whose paths reach the test's covering folders (median 15 % of last week's integrations against 72 % for a test-project hold); flaky and environment failures get a 7-day report-only quarantine. The automatic project-wide pre-merge fallback after two hours is removed in favour of a per-incident ladder with owner items. A line guardian role classifies reds, chooses quarantine, revert or fix forward, puts the repair first with a model rung, and lifts on evidence, reviewed by six weighted criteria. One test envelope with a fingerprint and a canary gives review, gate and post-merge runs the same world. Thirteen decisions, nine slices.

openDecisions.title: What stops the line
openDecisions.question: Which red results stop all integration of a project?

options.B: Build, prepare and the base suite confirmed twice

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Build, prepare and the base suite confirmed twice
openDecisions.rationale: The base suite defines a usable develop; every other red is a fact about one area.

openDecisions.title: When a quarantine starts
openDecisions.question: Who starts a per-test quarantine and on which evidence?

options.B: Held automatically on a routine test failing twice at the same SHA; report-only by the guardian on flaky or environment evidence

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Held automatically on a routine test failing twice at the same SHA; report-only by the guardian on flaky or environment evidence
openDecisions.rationale: The double failure is already measured; isolation must take minutes.

openDecisions.title: Where quarantines live
openDecisions.question: Repository file, server store or both?

options.A: Repository file written by a platform commit
options.B: Server-side store per project, read as a union with the file through one state route

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Server-side store per project, read as a union with the file through one state route
openDecisions.rationale: A commit would need the integration it protects, and .agent-studio/ is a global build input.

openDecisions.title: Duration and cap
openDecisions.question: How long may a quarantine last and how many at once?

options.B: Held 24 h plus one 24 h renewal while the repair is in progress; report-only 7 days; cap 3 held and 8 total

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Held 24 h plus one 24 h renewal while the repair is in progress; report-only 7 days; cap 3 held and 8 total
openDecisions.rationale: Long enough for one repair round, short enough to stay visible.

openDecisions.title: Who lifts, on what evidence
openDecisions.question: Who lifts a quarantine and what proves it may end?

options.B: Guardian on two consecutive passes on tips that contain the repair; owner at any time

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Guardian on two consecutive passes on tips that contain the repair; owner at any time
openDecisions.rationale: The evidence is mechanical; relapses within 7 days go to the owner.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Cards touching the test's covering folders or the confirmed suspect's paths; test project as fallback
openDecisions.rationale: A median of 15 % against 72 % of last week's integrations, and not wrong when the attribution is wrong.

options.A: Keep it with the AGT-3983 lane fact
options.B: Per-incident ladder with owner items at named points, no automatic project-wide step

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Per-incident ladder with owner items at named points, no automatic project-wide step
openDecisions.rationale: The fallback stopped all integration overnight for four non-regressions.

openDecisions.recommendation: B. A separate line guardian role whose holds the dispatcher honours

openDecisions.recommendation: B. Control at the last green SHA, two runs per point, stop on mixed, build only the failing test project
openDecisions.rationale: Removes the newest-merge bias at a bounded cost.

# RT-1 · No automatic project-wide fallback after two hours of red

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D7 (B), RT-D12 (B, the owner action is not part of this slice). Dependencies: none.

## Why
Dossier sections What exists and After the first red. `PostMergeModeService.EscalationActive` resolves a post-merge project to `pre-merge` when the attribution repair card is Escalated or develop has been red for two hours; `RedDevelopRepairPolicy.Decide` returns Escalate first at two hours whatever the repair lane, and the escalation moved a repair card out of Auto Review and superseded its review. The two-hour constant exists twice (`RedDevelopRepairPolicy.cs:17`, `PostMergeModeService.cs:47`). AGT-3983 (in delivery when the Dossier was written) adds the repair lane as a fact and removes `ReopenOriginal`; build on it if it has landed, otherwise include the lane fact yourself.

## Deliver

Remove the time rule and the escalated-repair rule and the duplicated constant. `RecordPostMergeAttributionEscalation` no longer sets a fallback; keep `AttributionEscalatedTaskId` readable for compatibility but ignore it for placement.
2. `RedDevelopRepairPolicy`: the facts include the repair card lane and the incident age. The decision vocabulary becomes Revert, FixForward, Hold and AskOwner. A repair in Auto Review (including gate queue and execution), Human Review, waiting for integration, Completed or Archive is Hold. At two hours of incident age the decision is AskOwner, never a lane move.
3. AskOwner creates one Needs you item per incident (dedupe by fingerprint) with the evidence of the latest red receipt and the options revert the attributed merge, keep fixing forward, or switch the project to `strict`; the recommended option is revert when exactly one clean independent suspect exists, otherwise keep fixing forward. The owner's answer is applied through existing routes; switching to `strict` stays an owner action.
4. No automatic code path moves a card out of Auto Review, Human Review or Completed because of a red develop, and no completed suspect is reopened.
5. Rewrite the fallback paragraph in `docs/system/domains/pipeline.md` (Per-project integration test placement, Red develop repair). Add one row for `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` to `docs/start/README.md`.

# RT-2 · Red test triage policy in the decision library

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D1 (B), RT-D2 (B), RT-D4 (B), RT-D5 (B), RT-D6 (B), RT-D7 (B), RT-D9 (B). Dependencies: RT-1.

**Area:** `orchestration-decisions/` only (new `RedTestTriagePolicy`, `HoldScopePolicy`, `BisectVerdictPolicy` or one cohesive set of files) and their tests

## Why
Dossier sections Principle, Quarantine, Scope of the hold, After the first red, Line guardian (classification rules) and Cost. All of the triage behaviour must be pure, replayable and in one place before any host applies it.

## Deliver
1. Typed facts for one failing test: test id, suite id and category (`base`, `routine`), first result, same-SHA repeat result, envelope canary result, fingerprint equal to the reference envelope, reference-envelope repeat result, control results at the last green SHA (0 to 2), bisect point verdicts, active quarantines of the project (kind, counts), distinct flaky runs in 14 days, relapse information, repair card lane, ages, build or prepare failure.
2. Classification: Flaky, Environment, Regression, WrongAttribution, Ambiguous, Inconclusive, exactly as the Dossier's classification table.
3. Decisions: LineStop (build, prepare, or base test failing twice; never quarantined automatically), StartHeld, StartReportOnly, CountFlaky, MarkInconclusive, Renew (once, 24 h, only while the repair is in progress), Lift (two consecutive passes on tips that contain the repair integration), AskOwner (reason, options, recommended option, for: line stop 60 min, renewal limit 48 h, cap exceeded, relapse within 7 days, T2 request), ProposeRevert, FixForward with a model rung (regression high, environment and flaky medium, one rung up on a second attempt).
4. Bounds as named constants in one place: held 24 h plus one 24 h renewal, report-only 7 days, cap 3 held and 8 total per project, flaky threshold 3 distinct runs in 14 days, relapse window 7 days, line-stop ask after 60 minutes.
5. Bisect verdicts: a point is Fail when both runs fail, Pass when both pass, Mixed otherwise; Mixed stops the search with class Flaky; a control that fails at the last green SHA attributes no merge.
6. `HoldScopePolicy`: hold paths are the covering folders of the failing test file (exact directory match) plus the test file plus the confirmed suspect's changed paths; no folders or more than 12 means fall back to the suite area; `MayIntegrate(changedPaths, holds, cardId)` exempts the repair card, a revert card of the attributed merge and an owner-exempt card. Revert independence: a later first-parent merge is coupled when it touches a file the suspect touched.
7. Keep `RedDevelopRepairPolicy` callers working (delegate or adapt); no host wiring in this slice.

## Acceptance
- Table-driven tests reproduce the Dossier's four reds of 22 and 23 November (AGT-3975, AGT-3980, AGT-3981, AGT-3983) as facts and get Flaky, Flaky, Environment and Environment, none LineStop.
- A base test failing twice gives LineStop; a fourth held test gives AskOwner with the cap reason; a relapse gives AskOwner.
- Bisect: control pass, points Pass, Fail gives Regression at the first Fail; any Mixed gives Flaky.
- Boundary guard tests stay green.

# RT-3 · Attribution protocol, covering folders and envelope fingerprint in the post-merge run

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D9 (B), RT-D6 (B, covering folders), RT-D10 (B, fingerprint part only). Dependencies: RT-2.

# RT-4 · Quarantine store, develop state with counts and the incident ladder

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D2 (B), RT-D3 (B), RT-D4 (B), RT-D5 (B), RT-D7 (B), RT-D11 (B, API part). Dependencies: RT-2, RT-3.

## Deliver
1. A server-side quarantine store per project beside `PostMergeRunStore`, with the AGT-W57 entry fields plus `kind` (`held`, `report-only`), `startedBy`, `startedAtUtc`, `incidentFingerprint`, `evidenceRunIds`, `coveringFolders`, `renewals`, `liftedBy`, `liftEvidence`; resolved entries are kept, never deleted. 2. API: `GET /api/projects/{name}/test-quarantines`, start, renew and lift routes for the system principal (until RT-8) and the owner; lift without evidence is owner-only. # RT-6 · One test envelope for review, gate and post-merge runs

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D10 (B). Dependencies: RT-5.

**Area:** a shared envelope definition in `contracts/TaskServer.Contracts/`, `backend/Features/Pipeline/BuildTestGateRunner.cs` (process start), `runner/RemoteReviewWorkspace.cs`, `runner/PostMergeRunCommand.cs`, `runner/WorkerCgroup.cs`, `.agent-studio/project.yml` (base filter), one new base test

## Why
Dossier section Environment parity. The review clears and allowlists its environment, the gate inherits the backend's, and post-merge clears with a different allowlist since AGT-3981; cgroups and processor counts differ in all three.

## Deliver
1. One allowlist builder used by all three: tool and OS variables, the project's declared `environment`, a run-owned `HOME` and temp root, no daemon, provider or Git credential variables. The gate's process start stops inheriting the backend environment.
2. One resource shape on Linux: a fresh worker cgroup leaf per test command with `cpu.max` equal to one gate token (3 cores, configurable) and `DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT` set to the same value in review, gate and post-merge. Where a host cannot delegate, record that in the fingerprint instead of failing.
3. Envelope fingerprint (RT-3 fields) on review and gate receipts too, and a `reference` envelope definition used by the RT-3 reference repeat.
4. A base test (for example `TestEnvelopeCanaryTests`, in the `backend-base` filter) that asserts from inside the test process: no `RUNNER_*`, `AGENT_HOST_*` or provider variables, its own `HOME`, a worker cgroup on Linux, the processor count set. A canary failure makes the run Inconclusive through RT-2, never red.
5. Document the envelope in pipeline.md and runner.md.

## Acceptance
- A test that prints its environment and cgroup produces the same allowlist digest and resource shape in a review, a gate and a post-merge fixture run.
- Injecting `RUNNER_SERVER_URL` into the daemon environment leaves the canary green; forcing it into the declared environment fails the canary and the receipt is inconclusive.
- Base suite duration stays under its 600-second cap.

# RT-8 · Line guardian role in the persona team, in shadow

Source: `docs/red-test-isolation/index.html` (AGT-3988), sections named below, and its `workbench.json`. Decisions: RT-D8 (B), RT-D13 (B, shadow part). Dependencies: RT-5.

**Area:** `backend/Policies/personas/` (descriptor and revisions lock), `backend/Features/Personas/` (role, principal, allow list, budget, log, shadow record), model classification call

## Why
Dossier section Line guardian. Until this slice the RT-4 rules act as the system principal; the owner needs a named, reviewable role with rights, budget and a log, separate from the dispatcher.

## Deliver
1. A role `line-guardian` (kind `guardian`, aspect `delivery`, project-scoped) with the Dossier's charter, following the dispatcher role pattern if DS-5 has landed, otherwise the persona descriptor schema with a new kind.
2. Allow list of operations and tiers exactly as the Dossier's rights table; T2 operations become owner items with an expiry and use cap; non-grantable operations are refused by the policy step.
3. Budget: model work at most one classification per incident and 60,000 tokens a week per project; compute for confirmation, control and bisect at most 90 core-minutes per incident and 600 a week per project, counted from receipts; exhaustion stops model work and raises an owner item, the rules keep running.
4. Ambiguous classification: one schema-bound model call with the excerpt, envelope difference and suspect diff summary; it returns a class and evidence, never an action; the rules then decide.
5. Shadow mode per project: the guardian computes and logs its decisions on every receipt next to the applied system decisions; a project setting switches it live (owner only), after which its principal applies RT-4's operations.
6. Log entries with the `PersonaLogEntryV1` fields; one feed item per closed incident.

## Acceptance
- In shadow, every receipt produces a guardian log entry and no applied change; after the owner switches a project live, quarantine and repair operations carry the guardian principal.
- A T2 request (quarantine a base test) becomes an owner item and is not applied.
- Budget exhaustion stops the model call and raises one owner item.
